..
Issued at 301 PM EDT Sat Aug 1 2026

Currently...Scattered to numerous showers and storms once again 
got going on the earlier side, and the many have already pushed 
south of the Orlando Metro and offshore Volusia coast, transiting 
the southern counties and approaching the coast from the Cape 
south. Between the early start and subsequent higher cloud cover, 
daytime heating hasn't been able to provide much instability and 
most convection has been rather mushy so far. A few gusts 25-35 
mph have been observed, as have pockets of 2" rainfall.

Rest of Today-Tonight...A low pressure system moving towards the 
Ohio Valley will deepen as a sharp trough cuts down south over the
Eastern US. While the low will finally lift the stalled front to 
our north away, moisture will begin surging across Florida in the 
wake of this system. In the few places that aren't clouded over, 
GOES imagery shows PWATs from 1.9-2.2" (75th to 95th 
climatological percentiles), backed by this morning's soundings. 
Values could push as high as 2.4" (near to exceeding 
climatological max), leading to a favorable environment for heavy 
rainfall leading to minor flooding, and the Weather Prediction 
Center has again outlined all of East Central Florida in a 
Marginal (level 1 of 4) risk for excessive rainfall. While most 
locations will see rainfall amounts 0.5" or less, a few spots will
get up to 2" , and one or two spots could see amounts over 3". 
The greatest potential for these higher amounts will be along the 
coast from the Cape south as activity collides with the sea 
breeze, which has barely managed to develop before being overrun. 
The highly saturated atmosphere isn't generally conducive to 
downdrafts, but water loading could produce gusty winds to around 
45 mph. Frequent lightning will also accompany the strongest 
storms. Forecast calls for high temperatures in the L90s, but 
those temperatures may be in the rear view mirror for places that 
already got heavy rainfall, if reached at all.

Sunday-Monday...The mid-upper level trough continues digging 
south over the Eastern US towards the Gulf and Florida Sunday, 
then the mid-level low becomes cut-off over the Tennessee Valley. 
The associated surface low elongates and weakens in response, but 
will help pull anomalously high moisture over the Florida 
peninsula in southwesterly flow between the low and high pressure 
east of Bermuda. Rain chances remain well above normal, especially
on Sunday which is shaping up to be pretty dreary, with multiple 
rounds of scattered to numerous showers and storms possible 
(chances up to 60-80%) and overcast skies. Highest chances will 
continue to be in the afternoons and evenings as the sea breezes 
attempt to form and daytime heating provides what little 
destabilization it can, but bands of vorticity transiting the base
of the trough aloft could support showers and storms in the 
overnights and mornings (chances 30% or less). More locations 
could see rainfall amounts up to 2" Sunday with the high coverage 
and repeated rounds, then more limited potential Monday as rain 
chances back off a bit. The Marginal (level 1 of 4) risk for 
excessive rainfall will continue for all of East Central Florida 
through Monday. Temperatures are forecast to be near to slightly 
below normal (if you can believe that) in the U80s-L90s thanks to 
the rain and cloud cover. Peak afternoon heat indices even dip 
into the 90s across most of the area Sunday, then up to the 
L-M100s Monday.

Tuesday-Friday...Return to more typical mid-Summer conditions. The
cut-off mid-level low lingers over the Appalachians before getting
swept up by a broad trough swinging across Canada and the northern
US mid-week, returning more seasonal broad ridging overhead. At
the surface, the ridge axis of the Atlantic high lifts back
towards Florida and eventually north of the area, shifting winds
southerly Tuesday into Wednesday, then onshore again late in the
week. The plume of anomalously high moisture is expected to linger
across Florida through mid-week, before more easterly flow ushers
it westward towards the Gulf, but will continue to see near to
above normal moisture advected across the peninsula in the onshore
flow. Rain chances remain above normal for most of the area,
generally 40-70% each afternoon-evening, with the highest chances
shifting towards the interior as the east coast sea breeze is able
to push farther inland each day. Can't rule out some minor
flooding concerns, but the threat looks to be closer to that
typically from our afternoon thunderstorms. While technically
warmer conditions are forecast as rain chances decrease some,
temperatures will be very near normal with afternoon highs mostly
in the U80s-L90s, pushing towards the M90s inland in some spots.
Peak heat indices generally 101-105, but a few locations could
perk towards 107. HeatRisk impacts Minor to Moderate.
